description: CT-10 — 'Device clock set 3 hours ahead. Pass criterion: HLC ordering preserved; skew alerted; original timestamps retained.' These vectors grade the ORDERING half, which is the part that must be byte-identical on client and server. Skew alerting and timestamp retention are server-side behaviours proved by test/sync-protocol.e2e-spec.ts, not by a shared corpus.

sequence.description: The skewed device's first operation. l' == l_msg, so the server's clock is dragged forward by three hours and c' = c_msg + 1. This is the algorithm as written; bounding it (GD-D1-03) is DEFERRED and deliberately not implemented, so this expectation must not be 'corrected'.
The device's second operation, one logical tick later. l' == l == l_msg -> max(c, c_msg) + 1. Causality between the device's own two operations survives the skew.
A healthy device on the same branch keeps producing operations at real time. Its own two operations remain correctly ordered relative to each other regardless of the skewed peer.

ordering.description: The skewed device's operations sort AFTER the healthy device's. That is the honest, detectable consequence of a wrong clock — not a defect in the algorithm — and it is exactly why FR-OFF-042 requires the skew to be recorded and the branch manager alerted.
The skewed device's own two operations remain in the order it produced them.
